chapters.summary: Chair Farah N. Louis announces the meeting is hybrid, explains how the public can testify in person or via Zoom, directs remote registration to the Council website, and notes the two-minute limit and written testimony email.
chapters.title: Chair Louis opens meeting and explains remote public testimony process

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: The meeting is being held in hybrid format.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Members of the public who wish to testify may testify in person or via Zoom.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Members of the public wishing to testify remotely may register by visiting the New York City Council website at www.council.nyc.gov backslash land use.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: To sign up,

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Or for those of you here in person, please see one of the sergeant at arms to prepare and submit a speaker card.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Members of the public may also view a live stream broadcast of this meeting at the council website.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: When you are called to testify before the subcommittee.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: If you are joining us remotely, you will remain muted until recognized by myself to speak.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: When you are recognized, your microphone will be unmuted.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: We will limit public testimony to two minutes per witness.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: If you have additional testimony that you would like to submit,

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: to the subcommittee, you would like the subcommittee to consider, or if you have written testimony that you would like to submit instead of appearing in person, please email it to landyoustestimony at council.nyc.gov.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Written testimony may be submitted up to three days after the hearing is closed.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Please indicate the LU number and project name in the subject line of your email.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: We request that witnesses joining us remotely remain in the meeting until excused by the chair, as council members may have questions.

chapters.summary: Chair Louis states that decorum must be observed, members of the public may not speak unless testifying, the witness table is reserved for called witnesses, and no video or photography is allowed from the witness table.
chapters.title: Chair Louis outlines decorum and witness table rules

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Lastly, for everyone attending today's meeting, this is a government proceeding and decorum must be observed at all times.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: of the public or acts not to speak during the meeting unless you are testifying.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: The witness table is reserved for people who are called to testify and no video recording or photography is allowed from the witness table.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Further, members of the public may not present audio or video recordings as testimony, but may submit transcripts of such recordings to the sergeant at arms for inclusion in the hearing record.

chapters.summary: Chair Louis opens the public hearing on LU 141, application D 2550162086 SWQ by Tiro de Esquina NYC Corp, for four tables with attached bench seating outside a restaurant in Corona, Queens. She notes Council Member Thomas-Henry has no remarks.
chapters.title: Chair opens public hearing on LU 141 sidewalk café application

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: I will now open the public hearing on LU 141 relating to the Sidewalk Cafe application 5 by Pedro de Esquina, NYC Corp, and Councilmember Thomas Henry's district.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Applicant is seeking to place four tables with attached bench seating.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Outside the front of its restaurant, which is located in Corona, Queens.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: For anyone wishing to testify regarding this proposal remotely, if you have not already done so, you must register online by visiting the council's website at council.nyc.gov backslash land use.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: For anyone with us in person, please see one of the sergeant at arms to submit a speaker card.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: If you would prefer to submit written testimony, you can always do so by emailing it to land use testimony at council.nyc.gov.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Councilmember Thomas Henry does not have remarks at this time.

chapters.summary: Chair Louis calls the applicant panel consisting of Christian Zuluaga, apologizes for mispronouncing his name, and asks council staff to administer the oath. Staff asks Zuluaga to raise his right hand, state his name, and swear to tell the truth.
chapters.title: Chair calls applicant Christian Zuluaga and administers oath

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: I will now call the applicant panel for this proposal, which consists of

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Krishtehan Zulwanga.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Sorry if I butchered your name.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Council, could you please administer the oath?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Zuluaga
utterances.text: Hello, can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Yes, good morning.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Zuluaga
utterances.text: Good morning, how are you?

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Hopefully you're not currently moving because I'm going to ask you to raise your right hand and state your name for the record.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Can you state your name for the record?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Zuluaga
utterances.text: Christian Zuluaga.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Do you swear to tell the truth and nothing but the truth in your testimony this morning and in response to council member questions?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Zuluaga
utterances.text: Yes, I...

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: You may make your statement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Zuluaga
utterances.text: Yes, I'm going to tell the absolute truth, the statements being the absolute truth.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: No, no, thank you.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: You can lower your hand and you've already sworn.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Do you have anything to testimony that you would like to share with us today?

chapters.summary: Christian Zuluaga says the application is to accommodate a seating area around the location. He describes the business as a restaurant-bar concept and family-friendly place selling food and beverages, and says the outdoor café tables will accommodate business operation hours.
chapters.title: Applicant Zuluaga presents restaurant and outdoor café plan

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Zuluaga
utterances.text: Well, basically, yeah, so we had to submit the application to be able to accommodate some seating area around our

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Zuluaga
utterances.text: location.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Zuluaga
utterances.text: Our cafe is a restaurant.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Zuluaga
utterances.text: Restaurant bar concept.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Zuluaga
utterances.text: It's a family joinable place where we offer and sell

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Zuluaga
utterances.text: food, beverage, liquid, and different type of products within a restaurant area.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Zuluaga
utterances.text: So the concept of the cafe tables outside exterior side of the building will just accommodate our business operation hours.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Zuluaga
utterances.text: And as I say, that's pretty much it.

chapters.summary: Chair Louis thanks the applicant and recognizes Council Member Thomas-Henry. Thomas-Henry asks for clarity on the entity managing outdoor dining, noting confusion between Tiro de Esquina and Cali Tajadas. Zuluaga explains the corporation started as Cali Tajadas 2 Corp and switched to Tiro de Esquina NYC Corp for a sports-bar concept.
chapters.title: Thomas-Henry questions applicant on business entity managing café

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: I don't have any questions for the applicant.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: I will now recognize Councilmember Thomas Henry for questions.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: How are you doing?

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: My first question is in regards to just getting clarity on the entity that will be managing

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: this outside dining, because there is, I have Tiro de Esquina and then DBA

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Calie Tejadas, and the way that business is set up, it appears that there's almost like two or three different entities or like,

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: What part of the business do you control and operate that will be managing the cafe?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Zuluaga
utterances.text: Okay, so basically I'll tell you a little story about the business.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Zuluaga
utterances.text: So we start the corporation as Cali Tejadas 2 Corp.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Zuluaga
utterances.text: The concept of the cafe was to start selling some bakery concepts and expanding the business on the bakery side.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Zuluaga
utterances.text: Unfortunately, the concept did not work.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Zuluaga
utterances.text: So we then switched the corporation name to T-Row the Skinner NYC Corp.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Zuluaga
utterances.text: As changing the concept of the restaurant to promote

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Zuluaga
utterances.text: this past World Cup, promoting to the football, the soccer, the sports concept.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Zuluaga
utterances.text: So we began as Cali Tejadas, but then the corporation names changed to Tiro de Esquina.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Zuluaga
utterances.text: So that's probably why the confusion or the name is getting mixed up together.

chapters.summary: Council Member Thomas-Henry asks for the current hours of operation. Zuluaga says the restaurant is open from noon to midnight, closed on Mondays, and open Tuesday through Sunday from noon to midnight.
chapters.title: Thomas-Henry asks about hours of operation

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: And what are the current hours of operation?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Zuluaga
utterances.text: Coverage hour for operation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Zuluaga
utterances.text: We are open from 11 a.m.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Zuluaga
utterances.text: 12 noon to 12 midnight.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Zuluaga
utterances.text: We are closed on Mondays.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Zuluaga
utterances.text: But every Tuesday to Sunday, we are open from noon to midnight, pretty much.

chapters.summary: Thomas-Henry asks whether most activity is indoors watching sports. Zuluaga confirms the business has a giant screen, attracted World Cup crowds, and that patrons watch sports indoors.
chapters.title: Thomas-Henry asks whether sports bar activity is indoors

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: And is it safe to assume as a sports bar, most of the activity is indoors and folks are inside watching different sports?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Zuluaga
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Zuluaga
utterances.text: So we have a giant screen, like a full screen to attract people seeking to see any kind of a sport.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Zuluaga
utterances.text: As I say, past World Cup, we were with good amount of neighborhoods, with neighbors, I'm sorry, and people coming from different places just to join and be able to see sport.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Zuluaga
utterances.text: Through the TVs or through the main concert is just watching the sports indoors.

chapters.summary: Thomas-Henry asks who the outdoor dining patrons will be. Zuluaga describes soccer-themed benches and tables outside where kids can eat with parents and play with a small soccer ball on the table surface, not outside the table.
chapters.title: Thomas-Henry asks who will use outdoor dining space

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: So I guess my question in that regard is, what do you anticipate as the patrons who would be using the outdoor dining space?

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Like traditionally, some people may choose to eat outside, but since you guys are mainly a sports bar where people come to watch the games, what do you anticipate?

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Who will be outside?

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Would it be?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Zuluaga
utterances.text: So we have some like a soccer kind of benches tables outside where kids go and have the opportunity to have a table, eat with their parents.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Zuluaga
utterances.text: But at the same time, in the lower piece of the table, there's like a soccer, a small field within the table itself where they can

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Zuluaga
utterances.text: actually play with a soccer ball by the foots.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Zuluaga
utterances.text: On the table, they just ate and shared.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Zuluaga
utterances.text: food, but it's just within the table itself.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Zuluaga
utterances.text: It is not outside of the table.

chapters.summary: Thomas-Henry asks whether the current colorful benches and turf setup will continue or be enclosed. Zuluaga says it will remain the same setup and will be removed in winter because it is fully exposed to snow and weather.
chapters.title: Thomas-Henry asks if outdoor setup will remain same

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Got it.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: And I have seen the setup.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: So that would be the same setup, what you have out there now with the colorful benches and the turf would be the same setup?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Zuluaga
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Or would you enclose it or would it continue to be set up the way it is?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Zuluaga
utterances.text: It will continue to be set up the way it is.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Zuluaga
utterances.text: Unfortunately, by when the winter comes in, we're just going to have to remove it because it's fully exposed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Zuluaga
utterances.text: Otherwise, it's going to be covered with snow or other exterior factors.

chapters.summary: Thomas-Henry notes precinct noise complaints and asks whether the applicant contacted neighbors on the avenue. Zuluaga says they spoke with neighbors, that noise comes from a second-floor event room with Zumba or dancing, that it is not daily, and that they offered to enclose windows.
chapters.title: Thomas-Henry questions applicant on noise complaints and neighbor outreach

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: So we have received some, well, we did check with the local precinct, and there have been some noise complaints.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Have you guys made any attempt to contact the neighbors off of a hunt on the app?

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: avenue, not on 104th Street side, but the homes on the avenue to let them know that you're interested in making.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Zuluaga
utterances.text: Yes, and we actually had come together with the neighbors and talked to them around it, and especially the noise

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Zuluaga
utterances.text: of lately complaints that have happened is because in the second floor,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Zuluaga
utterances.text: In the second floor, there's an event room.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Zuluaga
utterances.text: And there's some occasion where there's a Zumba class or dancing, but it doesn't interfere within operational hours.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Zuluaga
utterances.text: We have provided with options to fully enclose the windows, but it's just not happening as an everyday routine.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Zuluaga
utterances.text: It's just events from time to time that are taking place on the second level.

chapters.summary: Thomas-Henry asks whether security is present while open. Zuluaga says there is no front security guard, notes a separate rear bar called Sophia's Bar that causes confusion, and says the family restaurant does not need a security guard at the door.
chapters.title: Thomas-Henry asks about security at restaurant

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Do you have security while you're open?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Zuluaga
utterances.text: We don't have a front security man in the outbeat by our operation hours.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Zuluaga
utterances.text: But there's actually, so there's actually like the building itself, I'm sure you have seen it, there's actually a rear side of the building that operates as a full bar, Sophia's Bar,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Zuluaga
utterances.text: that has nothing to do with us.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Zuluaga
utterances.text: Having said, they do offer, and this is something that is highly affect our business since day one, because they do a different type of operation that

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Zuluaga
utterances.text: I don't have to tell the story or anything, but

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Zuluaga
utterances.text: That business alone had been actually front-faced by our neighbors, and most neighbors in our area just confused of which business are we in.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Zuluaga
utterances.text: Being that said, our business main door is on the other side of the building.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Zuluaga
utterances.text: But we, as being as a restaurant, concept, family, openable, kids-friendly scenario, we actually haven't

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Zuluaga
utterances.text: need a security guard in front of the door.

chapters.summary: Chair Louis asks whether Sophia's Bar ever uses the outdoor tables. Zuluaga says none of their tables are used by Sophia's Bar, which has a separate entrance and is totally separate from the business.
chapters.title: Chair Louis asks whether Sophia's Bar uses outdoor seating

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: And does Sophia's Bar use your tables at all, ever?

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: The outdoor seating?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Zuluaga
utterances.text: No, none.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Zuluaga
utterances.text: None of our tables.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Zuluaga
utterances.text: They have a separate entrance inside the business.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Zuluaga
utterances.text: They totally separate from our business.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Okay.

chapters.summary: Chair Louis thanks Council Member Thomas-Henry and the applicant, excuses the panel, and thanks Christian Zuluaga for making time to testify.
chapters.title: Chair thanks and excuses applicant panel

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Thank you, Councilmember.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: All right, this panel is excused.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Thank you so much for making time to testify.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Today, we appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Christian Zuluaga
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: You're welcome.

chapters.summary: Chair Louis makes a last call for remote and in-person public testimony. No members of the public wish to testify, so she closes the public hearing on LU 141 relating to the sidewalk café application by Tiro de Esquina NYC Corp.
chapters.title: Chair closes public hearing on LU 141 after no public testimony

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: This is the last call.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: If there are any members of the public who wish to testify regarding this proposal remotely, please press the raise hand button now, or if you are in person, please identify yourself to one of the sergeant at arms.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: This is the last call.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Being that there are no members of the public who wish to testify regarding LU-141 relating to the sidewalk cafe application by Teto de Esquina, NYC Corp, the public hearing is now closed.

chapters.summary: Chair Louis states that the item is laid over.
chapters.title: Chair lays over LU 141

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: This item is laid over.

chapters.summary: Chair Louis thanks members of the public, colleagues, subcommittee council, land use and council staff, and the Sergeant at Arms for participating. She adjourns the meeting.
chapters.title: Chair concludes business and adjourns meeting

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: That concludes today's business.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: I would like to thank the members of the public, my colleagues, subcommittee council, land use and council staff, and the Sergeant at Arms for participating in today's meeting.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: This meeting is hereby adjourned.

summary: Subcommittee on Zoning and Franchises held a public hearing on LU 141, a sidewalk café application for Tiro de Esquina NYC Corp at 45-18 104th Street in Corona, Queens.
Applicant Christian Zuluaga testified about the restaurant's sports-bar concept, outdoor soccer-themed seating, hours of operation, and neighbor noise concerns.
Council Member Shanel Thomas-Henry questioned the applicant on the business entity, hours, outdoor use, noise complaints, and security; no public testimony was offered, and the item was laid over.
title: Subcommittee on Zoning and Franchises
topic: Zoning, Cali Tajadas Bakery & Restaurant, Queens (D 2550162086 SWQ)
